problem: Prior legged-robot navigation work optimizes single skills (walking, short-range navigation) and does not integrate open-vocabulary detection with LLM task planning for long-horizon object search; real-world motion blur, jitter and target loss from legged locomotion break detectors.
motivation: Legged robots have strong terrain mobility, and LLMs plus open-vocabulary detectors offer planning and perception, but no operational system combines them for long-horizon open-world object navigation. Locomotion-induced blur makes detection fail even when the target is in view, so a stabilization and search-recovery mechanism is needed.
key_idea: A modular system where an LLM decomposes long tasks into subtask instructions, a YOLO-11 detector fed with Laplacian-variance-filtered frames finds the target, and a small transformer Language-to-Motion Model maps instruction, bounding box and states to velocity commands and search/mission states.
insight: Rejecting blurred frames (Laplacian variance threshold 150) and adding a 4th state (bidirectional search) sharply reduces search effort: for the backpack at 6 m, Ns 5.95 to 1.00 and Ts 178 s to 32.57 s (Table 3). Ablations show [SEP] tokens are essential for following commanded speed (eps_v 29.5 without vs 1.80), and motion-loss weight beta must be balanced (beta=20 fails). A tiny model (3.3M) trained on synthetic LLM-generated data suffices.
method: LLM task planner: DeepSeek R1 turns the user's long-horizon task plus L2MM feedback into basic mission instructions I_ins.
Instruction Object Extractor (IOE): a 2-layer transformer (dim 64) mapping an instruction to a detector class.

Laplacian variance blur filter: grayscale, Laplacian, variance below T_blur=150 marks the frame as blurred and it is replaced by the last clear frame; moving-average filter smooths boxes and confidences.
Open-vocabulary detector: YOLO-11 outputs class, confidence, normalized box center and size.

L2MM: encoder-decoder transformer (dim 256, 4 layers, 8 heads) over [SEP]-separated inputs (previous/current instruction, object, confidence, box, mission state, search state) with three heads: motion vector [vx,vy,theta] (MSE, beta=10), mission state and search state (cross-entropy; searching_0 rotates left, searching_1 rotates right).
Functional execution logic: rules for new mission, run to object, search for lost object, maintain state, and accomplish mission when the box size passes a success threshold.
Synthetic dataset: LLM-generated synonyms, instruction paraphrases and per-category success thresholds, 1M samples generated in under 15 min on CPU.

setting.backbone: DeepSeek R1 (frozen planner) + YOLO-11 (pretrained detector) + L2MM/IOE small transformers (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: 1M synthetic LLM-generated samples (4:1 train/test split); about 1 h training on an RTX 3080 Ti
setting.observation: monocular RGB video (robot built-in camera / RealSense D435i)
setting.action_space: continuous velocity commands [vx, vy, yaw rate] plus discrete search/mission states

numbers.eval_set_note: 4 scenes (ParkingLot, UrbanCity, UrbanRoad, SnowVillage), 100 trials each, max 500 steps
numbers.extra: 1.5 hours training; tracking-style benchmark (Episode Length / SR)

numbers_note: Only benchmark is Gym-Unreal tracking; SR is printed as fraction (1.00), kept as printed. Real-world results are qualitative or in ablation tables (Table 3).
results: On Gym-Unreal, LOVON reaches mean EL 499.75 and SR 1.00 with 1.5 h training, matching TrackVLA (500/1.00, 360 h) and beating EVT (487.75/0.94, 1 h). Real-world tests on Go2, B2, H1-2 show multi-goal long-horizon navigation, dynamic tracking and disturbance robustness.
limitations: Evaluated only on a target-tracking simulation benchmark and qualitative real-world demos, with no standard ObjectNav/VLN benchmarks or real-world success rates.
Purely reactive with no memory or map: search is just in-place rotation, so targets not reachable by turning in place are not handled; detection is limited to the closed class set of YOLO-11.
Blur threshold is empirically calibrated and the paper's own conclusion calls for integrating stronger VLMs.
